seal.statement: The production seven-node in-process cold-formation path used by the mandatory convergence probe completes all six joins and exposes ready table-scoped postgres-wire replicas through every admin endpoint inside the existing budgets by repairing the first violated owner-level liveness invariant; joining, publication, readiness, rebalancer, transport, quorum, and delivery safety remain unchanged, and a deterministic real-owner witness plus an exact source-revert control discriminates the repair before the unchanged full probe turns green.

text: The unchanged seven-node integration fails at committed main after approximately 483 seconds: node .605 exhausts two QUERYING_STATE service-registration retries with distributed participant failures, then the join path loses its self-WebSocket timer under shared-process pressure; .606 is not attempted.

The exact unchanged integration also fails at pre-attribution commit 0d545fec1 after approximately 502 seconds, reaching .606 before self-connect and admin timeouts. Formation attribution commits are therefore not the primary regression.

A diagnostic 30-second CPU profile at committed main attributes material formation cost to repeated os.cpus calls, readiness cache listeners, readiness evaluation, and semantic global projection. NodeService currently reads node.statsCollectionIntervalMs and stores lastStats but getNodeStats resamples host-wide CPU data on every heartbeat request, violating its configured statistics sampling boundary.

The focused NodeService owner witness is red before production edits: repeated getNodeStats calls ignore the injected deterministic host source and clock, produce distinct snapshots inside node.statsCollectionIntervalMs, and never invoke the expected owner sampler.

Restored NodeService use of its configured statistics sampling interval with a deterministic clock and host-stat source witness. The focused owner test passed, but the unchanged seven-node integration remained red at 496.9 seconds (64 assertions, 61 pass, 3 fail), so host sampling was contributory rather than the sufficient first liveness invariant.

Protected readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound witnesses reveal that same-key NODES heartbeat/lease updates are semantic no-ops whose global projection depends only on unchanged node identity, yet the tracker rebuilds and sorts all global control-plane rows for every such write. A 64-update deterministic witness is red on projection identity while all semantic classifications stay correct.

Reused the exact frozen global readiness projection across same-key NODES updates while retaining local liveness/load attribution and full rebuilds for membership insert/delete. All 761 registered readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound assertions passed, but the unchanged integration remained red at 497.0 seconds; it reached post-formation admin checks yet multiple per-node admin queries timed out under continuing parallel-query churn.

The readiness global projection consumes only the normalized nine-field SERVICES semantic row for membership fallback and priority topology, but exact timestamp-only same-key service refreshes still rebuild and sort the entire control-plane projection. A deterministic 64-refresh witness was red only on exact projection identity before the reuse change and now passes with all 745 protected readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound assertions.

All three unchanged convergence probes now converge on the same earlier owner-level failure: replica_operations-p1 retains four ACTIVE voters with two concentrated on the seed, no feasible spread target, and operation_ledger_quorum_concentrated blocks later provisioning. This corroborates the historical priority spread/drain residual and rules out treating parallel-query timeouts as the next write-substrate repair boundary.

Reused the exact frozen global readiness projection for same-key SERVICES updates whose complete canonical normalized row is unchanged. The 64-refresh deterministic witness and all 745 protected readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound assertions passed, but the unchanged three-file convergence lane remained red: the seven-node target reached 63/68 assertions before admin/readiness timeout, and both companion probes exposed replica_operations-p1 stuck at four voters with two on the seed instead of the three-voter target.

The deterministic real UnifiedRebalancer witness now reproduces the residual at sealed HEAD: SERVICES and the concentration owner report four ACTIVE operation-ledger voters across three nodes, the interaction owner mints ledger_surplus_drain, but terminal REPLACE history retires one still-live source from getCurrentReplicas and rebalance returns no_changes_needed with zero moves. Existing control and hold/cure/admission witnesses remain green, localizing the repair to replica projection under the already-authorized drain capability.

Fresh combined-candidate CPU profile (335 s sampled) still locates the dominant remaining load in readiness planning: cache observation/evaluation and direct global projection; ordinary service rows spent about 12 sampled seconds in full normalizeServiceRow calls just to identify priority membership, while selected priority services were normalized twice. Profile: /tmp/lagrange-seven-current-profile.wOsq39/CPU.20260909.062735.2118315.0.001.cpuprofile; diagnostic TAP: /tmp/lagrange-seven-current-profile.tap.

Added a deterministic work-count witness proving direct readiness projection prefilters ordinary services by partition identity and normalizes each selected priority service once. Clean red: /tmp/readiness-priority-service-prefilter-red-clean.tap (500/502; only new assertions failed). Implemented a single-pass priority-service projection with normalized partition-id prefilter. Targeted green: /tmp/readiness-priority-service-prefilter-green.tap (502/502). Paused before broader protected or exact convergence runs at owner request.

The single-pass priority-service projection passed all 1,077 readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound protected assertions (/tmp/readiness-protected-after-priority-service-prefilter.tap). The unchanged seven-node integration then reached joiner .604 READY but aborted at 182.2 seconds on the fixed 512 MB child heap limit while V8 was JSON-stringifying amid publication/replica-operation retry churn (22 assertions passed; /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-priority-service-prefilter.tap). This converts the remaining symptom from only timer starvation into directly observed allocation/retention pressure; the exact probe remains red.

Closed the measured duplicate-copy seam inside the existing canonical priority-census owner: authenticated frozen partition rows now build the local index without a second strict copy; ordinary services are classified by partition id before full normalization; the already-read partition ids are reused by census resolution. Deterministic 1000-partition/3003-service micro-repro improved from 1010.0 ms to 799.6 ms over 100 derivations (20.8%); focused real-owner and hostile-input suites passed 486/486 in /tmp/priority-census-copy-closure-green.tap; ESLint and diff check passed.

The correctly invoked unchanged classified seven-node probe cleared all six formation joins and reached .606 READY, then remained red in the admin tail: .602 websocket query and table-scoped discovery failed, .603 websocket query failed, and the child reached the fixed 512 MB heap limit at 469.2 s (75 assertions). Evidence: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-census-copy-closure.tap. The census copy closure materially advanced the formation phase but is insufficient; remaining load/retention starves distributed admin queries and eventually exhausts managed heap.

The latest unchanged probe OOM stack is in better-sqlite3 Statement.all while materializing a SQLite string, immediately after replica_operations operation-id reads. Historical release memory evidence saw only 25 final operation IDs/189,665 final steps_history bytes, but the unconditional parse memo retains up to 4,096 distinct historical string versions and their parsed graphs; because steps_history grows by prefix, the count-only memo can retain quadratic historical bytes invisible to the final-row census.

Added a deterministic growing-history witness for the existing steps_history computation memo. Clean red /tmp/steps-history-byte-bound-red.tap retained all 64 large historical versions under the entry-only cap (3 new assertions failed). The memo now preserves content-keyed newest-entry hits and value-equivalent reparse while evicting obsolete versions to a 4 MiB UTF-16 source-key bound. Green /tmp/steps-history-byte-bound-green.tap 9/9; adjacent liveness consumer /tmp/steps-history-byte-bound-adjacent.tap 44/44; ESLint and diff check pass.

The steps_history byte-bound rerun did not OOM but remained red earlier: joiner .605 exhausted its fixed attempts at 233.3 s after four joiners were READY, under the same distributed participant/query pressure. Evidence /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-history-byte-bound.tap. This supports the retention repair but rules it out as sufficient; return to the existing captured CPU profile for the next deterministic owner work-count seam.

Fresh post-fix CPU profile of the unchanged classified seven-node probe reached the fixed 480-second TAP deadline without OOM (67 runner assertions; .601-.604 READY, .605/.606 incomplete). The dominant remaining synchronous owner work is shadow-row materialization: readiness readRowsFromShadow spends 20.854 s self in per-row defineValue and storage-capacity readRows spends 15.409 s self in the same pattern. Profile: /tmp/lagrange-seven-current2.l9aUV6/CPU.20260909.073828.2143330.0.001.cpuprofile.

Added deterministic real-owner work-count witnesses. Clean red: readiness projection performed 130 per-row shadow array property definitions (/tmp/shadow-row-materialization-readiness-red.tap); storage partition attribution performed 128 (/tmp/shadow-row-materialization-capacity-red.tap). Replaced both loops with a shared captured-intrinsic Map-value materializer whose native CreateDataProperty path was 14.5x faster in a bounded 3000-row micro-repro and remains isolated from later iterator/prototype mutation. Focused greens: 504/504 and 46/46; protected readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound witnesses passed 1,168/1,168; ESLint, diff check, file-size ratchet, and impact-contract audit pass.

The unchanged exact seven-node integration after native shadow materialization completed every join: .601-.606 all reached READY, the aggregate ready assertion passed, and all six service-cache/routability pairs passed. It remained red in the admin tail at the fixed deadline: seed HTTP health passed, seed websocket query and table-scoped postgres-wire discovery failed, then .601 health timed out (61/65 assertions before TAP timeout; /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-native-shadow-materialization.tap). No OOM occurred. The repair moved the blocker from formation into loaded admin/query execution but is not sufficient for landing.

Added a deterministic row-local priority-service projection witness. Clean red /tmp/readiness-priority-service-row-local-red.tap proved one priority service update fully normalized all 128 priority service rows. The readiness projection now passes the exact old/new service row bracket into the table-impact owner, removes the prior semantic row, inserts only the changed priority row, sorts the preserved frozen slice, and falls back to a full rebuild on incomplete identity. Green and exact-full-rebuild parity pass; the protected eight-file readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound cone passes 1,173/1,173. ESLint, diff check, and the unchanged 27-file source-size ratchet pass.

Exact classified integration after row-local priority-service projection rebuild remained red: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-row-local-priority-service.tap, 67 assertions in 426862ms, SIGABRT after V8 heap exhaustion in JSON.parse at about 505 MB. Joiners .601-.605 reached READY; .606 failed all three attempts at its websocket self-connection under event-loop pressure. Seed and .601 passed health and admin websocket query; seed and .601 table-scoped discovery failed, .602 health passed, and its websocket assertion was the final assertion before OOM. This is materially deeper admin-tail progress than earlier runs but not exact green; no timing, retry, heap, cadence, or test budget changed.

Shared co-resident NodeService host-statistics sampling at the existing collection interval. The fresh CPU profile /tmp/lagrange-seven-current2.l9aUV6/CPU.20260909.073828.2143330.0.001.cpuprofile attributes 13.208s self to node:os cpus from heartbeat getStats (18.021s across all cpus frames): each logical NodeService in the seven-node process independently materialized the same host-wide CPU array. Added src/node/node-host-statistics-sampler.js, keyed by exact source and clock identity and storing only scalar host observations; node-specific identity, uptime, service/thread-pool counts, and timestamp remain per owner. Original source failed the real-owner test at /tmp/node-service-shared-host-sample-red.tap (113/117; two owners sampled twice, models diverged, boundary count shifted). Repaired source passes the expanded clock-isolation witness through the classified runner (150/150) and the related node/heartbeat/registration set (389/389). ESLint, git diff --check, file-size ratchet, and impact-contract registry pass. No cadence, timeout, retry, heap, or static budget changed.

Unchanged exact integration after shared host-statistics sampling remained red: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-shared-host-statistics.tap, 27 assertions in 228481ms, SIGABRT on V8 heap exhaustion. Joiners .601-.605 all reached READY; the process exhausted the existing 512 MB JS heap before .606 emitted a join assertion. This confirms the host sampler removes measured transient CPU/allocation work but is not the governing retained-state defect. No test, heap, timeout, retry, cadence, or static budget changed.

Heap snapshot /tmp/lagrange-heap-retention.NVcC0s/Heap.20260909.084346.2163055.0.001.heapsnapshot classifies the governing retention: the node-sql-parser root bundle retained one all-dialect SourceMap with 629,712 nested mapping arrays, while CDC recent-event retention was 1,210 entries and diagnostics value graphs were 0.36 MiB shallow. Lagrange supports only SQLite and PostgreSQL parser modes; the package's corresponding map files total 3,329,201 bytes versus 18,126,423 bytes for the root map.

Added a real SQLParser load-graph witness and replaced the node-sql-parser all-dialect root with its supported SQLite and PostgreSQL bundles. Original and exact source-only revert both fail 3/398 assertions: the root bundle is retained and the two configured owners are absent. Restored source passes 398/398; SQLite/PG/parser-property/dialect wiring pass 548/548; git diff check, unchanged file-size ratchet, and full quiet lint pass.

The unchanged exact seven-node integration after narrow parser ownership completed all six joins, all cache/routability assertions, and 31 of 33 admin-tail assertions without OOM: 90/92 TAP assertions passed in 446953ms. Only .605 table-scoped discovery (no successful snapshot) and .606 admin websocket query timed out; .606 discovery then passed. Evidence: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-narrow-parser-owners.tap. This validates the retained SourceMap repair but leaves synchronous distributed-query pressure inside the fixed deadline; no test, timeout, retry, heap, cadence, or static budget changed.

Fresh full-phase CPU profile /tmp/lagrange-seven-current3.3mSEIg/CPU.20260909.090750.2171272.0.001.cpuprofile (500.082 sampled seconds) identifies the remaining synchronous owner work: copyStrictOwnDataRecord 26.206s self, authoritative executeLocalQuery 24.649s self, node:os cpus 19.192s, authoritative equal-version JSON length ranking 11.412s, and projection canonicalRecordDigest 8.839s. Readiness evaluation is 132.444s inclusive. The leading strict-record cost is 8.016s from priority-partition summary canonical copies plus distributed readiness/liveness consumers.

Repaired the measured strict-record copy primitive without relaxing hostile-input admission. A deterministic owner work-count witness fails on original and exact source-only revert with 128 Object.defineProperty calls for one 128-field record; the null-prototype output now uses direct own data writes, yielding zero definition calls while preserving null prototype, all values, and writable/configurable/enumerable descriptors. Restored green: focused readiness/liveness/storage/projection set 1,256/1,256; protected readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound cone plus parser and utility witnesses 1,601/1,601; diff check, unchanged file-size ratchet, and impact-contract registry pass.

Bounded prepared-read ownership for the profiled authoritative local-query seam. Added one most-recent SELECT statement per exact SQLite database handle in a WeakMap; identical SQL reuses the statement with fresh parameters, a different SQL replaces it, writes remain uncached, and arbitrary query text cannot grow retained state. Original and exact source-only revert fail the real PartitionService witness by preparing the identical SELECT twice; restored source passes partition/CDC/metrics/direct-routing plus strict-record witness 318/318. Full quiet lint, diff check, and unchanged file-size ratchet pass.

Unchanged exact integration after bounded prepared-read ownership remained red at the fixed deadline: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-local-read-statement-owner.tap, 68/72 TAP assertions passed in 480900ms. All joins/cache assertions passed, but seed/.601 discovery had no successful snapshot, .602 admin query timed out, and TAP expired before later nodes. The deterministic statement reuse remains valid and bounded, but is not the governing convergence repair; no budgets or test source changed.

Closed the profiled authoritative equal-version row-ranking seam. Identical non-proxy plain/null-prototype rows with the same enumerable primitive own data and no JSON hook now prove equal serialized length without JSON allocation; nested, hooked, accessor, divergent, or version-ordered rows keep the prior path. Original and exact source-only revert serialize all 128 identical 16 KiB replica rows and fail the witness; restored source performs zero serializations, preserves first-copy selection, and keeps the divergent toJSON ranking witness green. Full CDC suite passes 1,759/1,759; lint, diff check, and unchanged file-size ratchet pass.

CDC identical-flat-row merge fast path is deterministic and exact-revert proven (authoritative owner test red with 128 serializations, green with zero; full CDC 1759/1759), but unchanged seven-node corroboration remains red: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-flat-row-rank-skip.tap, 46/54 pass in 495700ms; nodes .601-.604 ready, .605 routingReady false, .606 undiscoverable, repeated fixed one-second distributed-query timeouts. Optimization is not governing alone; continue profiling first remaining real owner without changing budgets.

The full-phase CPU profile attributes 34.417 sampled seconds to resolveMemoizedMembershipPublicationPlanningSnapshotForContextSync under buildRuntimeAuthoritySnapshot after resolveNodeMembershipPublicationPlanningAnswer had already performed the same direct/publication merge. A real ControlPlaneReadinessService work-count witness proves the async owner builds one completed frozen answer and its immediate runtime-authority consumer rebuilds the deep merge a second time under the same node, observedAt, and membership-publication identity.

Preserved the completed async membership-planning answer across its same-readiness-build owner seam, guarded by exact service, node, observedAt, and membership-publication identities; arbitrary or later snapshots retain the existing merge path. Original and exact source-only revert fail the work-count witness with two merge builds; restored source uses one and preserves answer identity. Focused readiness tests pass 1117/1117; the registered readiness-freshness-macrotask-bound cone plus witness passes 1202/1202; diff check, scoped lint, unchanged file-size ratchet, and impact-contract registry pass. Red: /tmp/cl-034-async-answer-single-merge-exact-source-revert-red.tap; green: /tmp/async-planning-answer-owner-focused-green.tap and /tmp/protected-readiness-after-async-planning-answer-pass-through.tap.

The unchanged seven-node corroboration after completed async planning-answer pass-through remains red at the fixed deadline: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-async-planning-answer-pass-through.tap, 67/73 passed. All six joiners reached READY; all cache, routability, local message-group, and admin-runtime assertions passed. The residual is isolated to the admin query tail: seed smoke query eventually passed, but table discovery and later websocket reads had no response under continuing background distributed-query saturation (138 parallel-query failures, chiefly the unchanged 1000ms internal timeout). No test, retry, timeout, cadence, heap, or static budget changed.

Post-pass-through CPU profile confirms the async membership-planning-answer repair collapsed resolveMemoizedMembershipPublicationPlanningSnapshotForContextSync/buildRuntimeAuthoritySnapshot from about 34.4 sampled seconds to about 0.221/1.246 seconds. Remaining dominant application work is rebalancer follow-up census/normalization (closure evidence about 14.3s inclusive; replica-operation progress/normalization about 15.3/14.7s) plus admin query execution. The profiling run is diagnostic only: it reached 65/66 before a 306s background distributed-write rejection, so it is not landing evidence.

The post-readiness profile's first remaining repeated owner seam was priority-recovery closure-witness evidence: one surrogate synthesis rebuilt the same decision census/ranking several times for one frozen planning snapshot, while the only live external dependency is the explicitly versioned replica_operations ledger.

Bounded repair: retain one closure-witness evidence generation per rebalancer, keyed by exact frozen planning-snapshot identity plus replica_operations mutation version; mutable caller snapshots and unversioned caches remain uncached. Deterministic real-owner witness was red before the change and on exact source-only revert (4 assertions fail), then green at 43/43; focused follow-up coverage is green at 387/387.

Unchanged seven-node integration after closure-evidence memo remains red but advances to 80/84 assertions within the same 482s test deadline. All seven nodes reach READY and all service/cache/runtime seams pass. Seed completes query and discovery; node .601 loses query and discovery, .602 loses query but completes discovery, .603 and .604 complete all admin checks, then the global deadline expires while entering .605. Remaining failure is solely intermittent fixed-1s admin-query tail latency.

The global topology-blocking operation view is an invariant of one system-table cache generation, but the existing memo was instance-local, so every co-resident rebalancer repeated the same full replica_operations scan and per-row progress reconstruction. Re-keyed the one-entry memo by shared cache only for canonical classifier methods; owners with overridden classifiers retain isolated per-instance memo semantics, and unversioned caches remain uncached. Real co-resident-owner witness is red before and on exact source-only revert (2 failures), then green; focused rebalancer coverage is green.

Unchanged seven-node integration after sharing the global topology operation view remains red at the same fixed deadline: 69/72 assertions pass. All seven nodes reach READY; seed completes all admin checks and node .601 websocket query succeeds, but .601 discovery and .602 query consume the remaining deadline. The admin frontier varies across exact runs while readiness remains green, classifying the remaining defect as CPU/event-loop starvation rather than a deterministic route-availability failure.

Fresh post-repair CPU profile confirms the shared global operation census removed the earlier progress-snapshot hotspot, but exposes a larger owner-local amplification: priority publication visibility handling consumes about 92s inclusive, including about 42s rebuilding current placement; normalizeControlPlanePublicationRow alone consumes about 14.3s self-time. The dominant normalizer callsites are active-node publication selection, where the recent published-baseline union is recomputed inside per-node retention checks.

The active-node projection's published-baseline retention owner recomputed and re-normalized the complete publication census inside each candidate-node check (29 publication-kind reads for seven nodes). It now resolves the recent published baseline once per projection and threads that immutable list through all retention and diagnostic branches (3 reads independent of node count), preserving the exact projected cohort. The witness is red before and on exact source-only revert, green at 104/104; adjacent projection/readiness coverage is green.

The fresh profile attributed about 12.7s of replica-operation normalization directly to isOperationForEntity while each entity owner scanned the shared ledger. Added an exact direct-entity-id rejection before workflow/timeline decoding, using the same snake-before-camel string precedence; matching or ambiguous rows still use the canonical normalizer. The hostile getter witness is red before and on exact source-only revert (unrelated history decoded), green after repair; focused rebalancer coverage is green.

The follow-up context owner scanned and decoded every replica_operations row before filtering to its requested partition (about 16.3s inclusive in the fresh profile). Extracted a single-pass census that applies the canonical partition-group/partition/entity field precedence as a cheap rejection only when an explicit string owner is present; ambiguous rows, matching rows, tracked-state classification, and time-based stale classification retain the old path. Hostile history witness is red before and on exact source-only revert (6 reads instead of 3), green after; 395 focused assertions pass.

The late-formation profile's dominant remaining synchronous owner path is publication visibility handling: each PUBLISHED cache callback evaluates the full priority operation-creation gate before entering the existing owner-key reconcile queue. A real UnifiedRebalancer/OwnerKeyReconcileQueue burst witness proves 64 identical publication events already coalesce to one pending owner while sealed behavior redundantly builds 64 planning gates.

Moved only the publication-listener planning-gate evaluation across the existing rebalance queue boundary. The listener records operation_creation_deferred_to_reconcile and enqueues conservatively; the coalesced checkRebalance owner evaluates the unchanged fail-closed gate once. Direct exact scheduling decisions retain the original planning gate. Deterministic witness is red before and on exact source-only revert (64 gate builds), green with zero callback gate builds and one pending owner; adjacent focused coverage passes 339/339.

Rejected and fully reverted publication-listener gate deferral. Although the deterministic real-owner burst reduced 64 synchronous gate builds to zero and focused tests passed, the unchanged seven-node corroboration regressed to a 128-second fixed-heap OOM after 27 assertions: conservative publication wakes scheduled substantially more full rebalance work than the filtered listener. No attempted source or test bytes remain. This rules out unconditional per-partition enqueue; retain the needs-operation filter and share or narrow its computation instead. Evidence: /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-publication-listener-deferral.tap and /tmp/priority-publication-listener-rejected-attempt-reverted.tap.

Inside the profiled priority publication gate, buildCurrentPriorityRecoveryPlanningSnapshot rebuilt the full current-placement observation before checking whether the published priority summary was already pending. In that pending branch the method discarded the observation and returned the exact original planning snapshot; the work had no semantic consumer.

Moved the published-pending identity return ahead of current placement reconstruction. Sticky satisfied publication still performs the actuator overlay, while an already-pending authoritative summary returns unchanged without touching placement. The real-owner witness is red before and on exact source-only revert (one discarded build), green with zero; adjacent focused coverage passes 219/219, file-size and lint pass.

Short-circuited current priority placement reconstruction when the authoritative published priority summary is already pending, preserving exact snapshot identity and all sticky-satisfied actuator overlay behavior. Deterministic real-owner and exact source-only revert proofs discriminate one discarded placement build versus zero; five focused rebalancer files pass 219/219. The unchanged seven-node classified integration is green for the first time: 94/94 assertions in 400601ms within the original 480-second timeout, with all six joins, READY states, routing/cache seams, websocket queries, and table-scoped admin discovery complete. Evidence: /tmp/pending-priority-placement-observation-exact-source-revert-red.tap, /tmp/pending-priority-placement-observation-focused-green.tap, /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-after-pending-placement-short-circuit.tap.

Finalized the exact candidate after semantic-preserving static refactors and the checker-directed cognitive-complexity ratchet tightening from 162 to 161. The final focused plus protected cone passes 2341/2341; the complete static gate passes; the unchanged, uninstrumented seven-node classified integration passes 94/94 in 237214ms inside the original 480-second timeout. The integration test is byte-identical to sealed HEAD and no timeout, retry, join-attempt, cadence, heap, or other budget changed. Evidence: /tmp/red-main-formation-final-focused-and-protected-green.tap, /tmp/red-main-formation-final-tightened-static-green.log, /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-final-candidate-third-run.tap.

Altitude check after 27 measured attempts: the candidate remains at the sealed owner-level liveness altitude. Each retained change removes repeated work or retained history inside an existing readiness, publication, rebalancer, CDC, storage, SQL, or host-statistics owner; rejected queue-boundary widening was fully reverted. The deterministic exact-revert discriminator, protected interaction cone, static gates, and unchanged seven-node probe now all align, so no higher-altitude Quest or goal change is warranted before aggregate verification and landing.

APPROVE: independently reviewed all 45 non-Quest paths against sealed HEAD, validated the corrected receipt and exact artifact hashes, confirmed the integration test blob is unchanged, and found owner boundaries, fail-closed safety, bounded caches, retry/cleanup behavior, and unchanged budgets intact. Fresh checks passed 1401/1401 owner/admission/readiness-pair assertions plus 1002/1002 remaining focused assertions, impact contracts, guidelines, unused exports, file size, changed-source ESLint, diff check, and Quest append-only audit. Residual hostile camel-alias accessor risk is non-blocking because isOperationForEntity receives internal SystemTableCache plain-data clones, not arbitrary caller objects.

The first guarded landing proof reached the broad exclusive suite and exposed a historical-test environment bug, not a formation regression: critical-placement-trace-classifier's trace-changes-no-behaviour asserted that the current working tree had no src delta, while Solver deliberately stages the source candidate before npm test. That made every sufficiently broad future source Quest fail the old S6a receipt invariant even though the trace changed nothing.

Repaired the historical S6a no-behaviour guard to inspect its immutable landing commit 5b4ae82dfbeff4d6cc9e1d7e944a8ca19de031fc with git diff-tree instead of demanding an empty current src working tree. This preserves the original observation-only proof while allowing Solver's staged-tree landing contract. The focused guard passes 8/8 with the current source candidate present; the complete static gate passes; owner inventories and the impact graph were regenerated from the candidate. No production source, integration test, timeout, retry, cadence, heap, or budget changed after the 94/94 exact integration pass. Evidence: /tmp/red-main-formation-staged-source-trace-guard-green.tap and /tmp/red-main-formation-post-landing-repair-static-green.log.

APPROVE: independently verified the exact 49-path aggregate after the landing-harness repair. The historical S6a guard now pins immutable landing commit 5b4ae82dfbeff4d6cc9e1d7e944a8ca19de031fc, whose src delta is empty, while passing 8/8 with this Quest's dirty source candidate. Both owner inventories and the impact seal reproduce byte-for-byte; the probe is 0/6 outstanding; fresh priority owner cone 219/219, impact proof cone 38/38, import graph 8/8, contracts, guidelines, ratchets, shards, append-only, syntax, and diff checks pass. Production bytes and the exact integration test remain unchanged since the verified 94/94 artifact.

After the post-landing DELETE/cache-absence repair, a fresh unchanged seven-node run reached five READY joiners but timed out on .606. The first causal burst preceded the final operation-ledger barrier: already-aligned authoritative catch-up UPSERTs minted cache mutation generations and woke every readiness/publication consumer, producing replica_operations/control_plane_publications ingress and query storms. The barrier remained correctly fail-closed and was not the root. The old critical-table-never-leaves-seed class remained solved by authoritative catch-up.

Completed the final systemic CDC repair set. Every successful DELETE, including zero-row durable idempotent success, now reasserts cache absence through a frozen leader-required owner-RPC authority with same-key race protection. Authoritative UPSERT repair now short-circuits only when the canonical cache row already satisfies the requested reconciliation mode, eliminating mutation-generation/listener feedback while retaining changed SERVICES routing-field repair and all DELETE behavior. Exact source-revert controls are red only on their target invariants; restored owner witnesses pass 50/50; regenerated static gates pass; the 34-file systemic cone passes 3168/3168; and the byte-identical seven-node probe passes 94/94 in 137570ms inside unchanged budgets. Evidence: /tmp/zero-delete-owner-gateway-module-final-exact-source-revert-red.tap, /tmp/aligned-authoritative-catchup-module-final-exact-source-revert-red.tap, /tmp/red-main-formation-idempotent-catchup-final-static.log, /tmp/red-main-formation-idempotent-catchup-final-refactor-cone.tap, /tmp/lagrange-seven-node-idempotent-catchup-final.tap.

REJECT: authoritative absence repair has two material cache-consistency gaps. The same-key race guard compares values, so an equal-value live mutation during the leader read can still be deleted; and the repair DELETE carries no causal version, so a late older CDC update can resurrect the row.
